content.title: About
content.content: Brazil nuts (Bertholletia excelsa) are large edible seeds from a tree native to the Amazon rainforest. Raw nuts have a mild, buttery flavor and a crunchy texture. They are eaten raw, roasted, or used in baking, confectionery, and for making oil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brazil nuts grow in massive pods that can contain 10–25 nuts each.
A single tree may produce up to 3,000 nuts per year, but it fruits only every 2–3 years.
They are one of the richest natural sources of selenium, an essential micronutrient for immunity and antioxidant protection.
The seeds are pressed to produce oil prized for its high smoke point and neutral taste.
In traditional Amazonian cuisine, nuts are often toasted over an open flame or added to soups and sauces.

items.title: Rich in selenium
items.content: One nut can meet the daily selenium requirement for an adult, supporting immune function and oxidative stress defense.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Most of the fat is monounsaturated and polyunsaturated, which are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids muscle and nerve function and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: Vitamin E and antioxidants help maintain skin elasticity and protect against damage.

items.title: Protein and fiber
items.content: Brazil nuts provide plant protein and dietary fiber, promoting satiety and digestive health.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Brazil nuts can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Excess selenium
items.content: Overconsumption may lead to selenosis, characterized by hair loss, brittle nails, and gastrointestinal issues.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: They are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole nuts can be a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Brazil nuts can be enjoyed as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or processed into nut butter. Light toasting enhances flavor, but raw nuts retain the most nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent oil oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid.
